subject: history
topicDisplay: World History Topic Causes Effects Of 20th Century Wars
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: Which Italian maritime republic played the dominant role in diverting the Fourth Crusade?
questions.explain: Venice, under Doge Enrico Dandolo, supplied the fleet and redirected the crusade first to Zara and then to Constantinople.

questions.q: The European witch craze is generally dated to which broad period?
questions.explain: The intensive phase of witch-hunting in Europe peaked between roughly 1580 and 1750.

questions.q: Which clause of the Treaty of Versailles assigned responsibility for the war to Germany and its allies?
questions.explain: Article 231, the 'war guilt clause', held Germany and its allies responsible for the war and provided the legal basis for reparations.

questions.q: Konrad Adenauer, the first Chancellor of the Federal Republic, led which political party?
questions.explain: Adenauer led the Christian Democratic Union (CDU), serving as the first Chancellor of West Germany from 1949 to 1963.

questions.q: The ideological and political division of Europe after 1945 between Western and Soviet spheres became known as the:
questions.explain: Churchill popularised the phrase 'Iron Curtain' in 1946 to describe the Soviet-imposed division of Europe during the Cold War.

questions.q: German reunification, when East and West Germany were formally united, took place in which year?
questions.explain: Germany was officially reunified on 3 October 1990, following the fall of the Berlin Wall in November 1989.

questions.q: Which development is most associated with the decline of witch persecutions after c1680?
options: The growth of scientific rationalism and judicial scepticism
The spread of the printing press
questions.explain: The rise of scientific rationalism and increasing scepticism among judges and elites undermined the legal basis for prosecutions.

questions.q: The Enabling Act, which allowed Hitler's government to pass laws without the Reichstag, was passed in which year?
questions.explain: The Enabling Act of March 1933 gave Hitler dictatorial powers to legislate without parliamentary or presidential approval for four years.

questions.q: The Weimar Republic's constitution, which established a federal democratic state, was adopted in which year?
questions.explain: The Weimar Constitution was adopted in August 1919, creating a parliamentary democracy with a directly elected President.

questions.q: Which factor is most commonly cited as intensifying the witch craze in the period of religious conflict?
options: Confessional rivalry between Protestants and Catholics after the Reformation
questions.explain: Reformation-era confessional anxiety and rivalry between Protestants and Catholics heightened fears of diabolical conspiracy.

questions.q: At which 1815 battle was Napoleon finally defeated, ending his Hundred Days?
questions.explain: Napoleon was decisively defeated at Waterloo on 18 June 1815 by Wellington and Blucher, leading to his exile to St Helena.

questions.q: The student resistance group active in Munich that distributed anti-Nazi leaflets in 1942-43 was known as what?
questions.explain: The White Rose, led by Hans and Sophie Scholl, distributed leaflets against the regime before its members were arrested and executed in 1943.

questions.q: The French and Belgian occupation of the Ruhr, prompted by Germany defaulting on reparations, began in which year?
questions.explain: French and Belgian troops occupied the Ruhr in January 1923 to extract reparations in kind, triggering passive resistance and hyperinflation.

questions.q: Roughly when did the Vietnam War's major US involvement intensify?
questions.explain: US combat involvement escalated sharply from the mid-1960s, following the 1964 Gulf of Tonkin incident.

questions.q: The Wall Street Crash, which precipitated the Depression that devastated Germany, occurred in which year?
questions.explain: The Wall Street Crash of October 1929 caused American loans to be recalled, plunging Germany into mass unemployment and economic crisis.

questions.q: The Brezhnev Doctrine asserted the right to do what?
options: Intervene in any socialist state threatening communism
questions.explain: The Brezhnev Doctrine (1968) claimed the right to intervene to protect socialism in bloc states.

questions.q: Which Nazi figure headed the SS and oversaw the apparatus of terror and the concentration camp system?
questions.explain: Heinrich Himmler, as Reichsfuehrer-SS, controlled the SS, the Gestapo and the concentration camps at the heart of the Nazi terror state.

questions.q: The Nuremberg Laws, which stripped German Jews of citizenship and banned marriage with non-Jews, were enacted in which year?
questions.explain: The Nuremberg Laws of 1935 institutionalised antisemitism, defining who was 'Jewish' and removing Jews' civil rights.

questions.q: The Berlin Wall, dividing the city for nearly three decades, was constructed by the East German regime in which year?
questions.explain: The East German authorities began building the Berlin Wall in August 1961 to halt the flow of refugees to the West.

questions.q: In which year did Soviet forces crush the Hungarian Uprising?
questions.explain: The Hungarian Uprising of 1956 was suppressed by Soviet tanks, ousting reformer Imre Nagy.

questions.q: Which Muslim leader recaptured Jerusalem from the crusaders in 1187?
questions.explain: Saladin defeated the crusaders at Hattin and retook Jerusalem in October 1187, triggering the Third Crusade.

questions.q: The Young Plan, which further reduced and rescheduled Germany's reparations payments, was introduced in which year?
questions.explain: The Young Plan of 1929 reduced the total reparations bill and extended the repayment period, though it provoked nationalist opposition.

questions.q: In which year was Louis XVI executed by guillotine?
questions.explain: Convicted of treason by the National Convention, Louis XVI was guillotined on 21 January 1793.

questions.q: Which Christian city did the Fourth Crusade sack in 1204?
questions.explain: Diverted from the Holy Land, the Fourth Crusade sacked the Byzantine capital Constantinople in April 1204.

questions.q: Germany was admitted to the League of Nations in which year, a diplomatic success for Stresemann?
questions.explain: Germany joined the League of Nations in 1926, becoming a permanent member of the Council and signalling its return to the international community.

questions.q: What was the popular name for the European Recovery Program of 1947-48?
questions.explain: The Marshall Plan provided US economic aid to rebuild Western Europe and resist communism.

questions.q: The murder of which socialist deputy in 1924 provoked a major crisis for Mussolini's regime?
questions.explain: The kidnapping and murder of Giacomo Matteotti in June 1924, after he denounced Fascist violence, triggered the Matteotti Crisis.

questions.q: The July Bomb Plot, an attempt by army officers led by Stauffenberg to assassinate Hitler, took place in which year?
questions.explain: The July 1944 Bomb Plot (Operation Valkyrie) failed to kill Hitler and was followed by brutal reprisals against the conspirators.

questions.q: In which year did US combat troops complete withdrawal from Vietnam?
questions.explain: Under the 1973 Paris Peace Accords, US combat forces withdrew from Vietnam.

questions.q: The Byzantine defeat at which 1071 battle helped prompt the appeal that led to the First Crusade?
questions.explain: The Seljuk Turks crushed the Byzantines at Manzikert in 1071, opening Anatolia to Turkish settlement and prompting the appeal to the West.
